Outline: Caelen completes his tactical assessment inside the cart, shifting from panic to a cold, transactional mindset as the vehicle approaches its destination. He observes the stranger’s posture—relaxed legs crossed, eyes shut—and deduces indifference over malice. The physical sensation of the cart’s suspension confirms the terrain is soft and yielding, suggesting high gravity or deep earth rather than a rough road. His internal monologue reframes his status: he is not a victim of monsters but an inventory item in a ledger that doesn’t yet exist for him. He tests his restraints mentally, noting the raw friction on his broad-palmed wrists and the dulled pain from previous beat trauma. The beat concludes with Caelen shifting into a state of hyper-vigilant stillness, conserving energy while mentally cataloging the cart's route and the captor's habits.
Prose:
The cart lurched forward, its suspension groaning under the weight of Caelen’s bound body. Every vibration traveled through him like a shockwave, amplified by the unfamiliar density of his new frame. Outside the slats of the cart, the world blurred into streaks of pale yellow. The stone wall he had woken beside slid backward, then vanished entirely, replaced by an endless expanse of hazy horizon and the low, dim sun. There were no mountains, no forests—only a flat, dusty expanse that seemed to stretch forever under the oppressive sky. The terrain was soft, yielding to the wheels, suggesting heavy gravity or simply deep, compacted earth. 

Caelen forced himself to stop struggling against the ropes. Resistance only invited more attention, and he had already been beaten into silence once. He lay still, conserving his energy, listening to the creak of the cart’s axle and the distant sound of hooves on gravel. A figure sat opposite him in the cart, legs crossed, eyes closed as if sleeping or ignoring him completely. Caelen watched the man’s profile noting the calluses on his hands, the practical cut of his tunic, and the lack of any insignia that might indicate rank or faction.

He tried to categorize the sensory input. This wasn’t a dream; there was too much weight here, too much pain. Yet the pain was distant now, dulled by the sheer absurdity of his situation. The air smelled of dust, old leather, and something metallic—blood or rust? He couldn’t tell. His mind struggled to categorize the sounds drifting from outside: harsh consonants and rolling vowels that made no sense in any language he knew.

He shifted slightly, testing the range of motion allowed by the cord binding his wrists. The friction left raw, stinging trails on his skin. He felt heavy, anchored down by gravity that felt stronger than anything he remembered from Earth.

Outline:
Purpose: Caelen wakes in the stone-walled pen, observing his captors shift from transactional indifference to active humiliation as he attempts a desperate social bluff to improve his conditions.

Viewpoint: Third-person limited (Caelen). The camera lingers on the grim texture of the enclosure—pale yellow light filtering through high slits, the rough skin of thirty others huddled in the shadows, and the heavy breathing of guards patrolling the perimeter.

Objective: Caelen must suppress his panic upon waking from the beat-induced unconsciousness. He assesses the immediate threat level: a masked man in purple undermines a scarred captive's authority while a guard strikes a distressed young woman. Caelen identifies an opening to intervene not through combat, but through a calculated social interaction with the guard, attempting to bluff his way into better treatment or at least less pain.

Meaningful Change: The narrative shifts from passive victimhood (transport) to active, albeit precarious, engagement within the slave pen. Caelen transitions from internal analysis of his status as "inventory" to external action, risking a moment of agency that contradicts his physical helplessness. He establishes a temporary dynamic with the guard where deception is the primary tool for survival.

Continuity Dependencies: This beat follows the cart ride ending in unconsciousness; Caelen is now alert but physically restrained by the collar and ropes. The scarred captive's standing must be visibly undermined by the man in purple to provide the context for Caelen’s intervention. The guard’s strike on the woman serves as the catalyst that forces Caelen to act, blending the established harshness of the world with his attempt at a quip-laden bluff.
Prose:
Caelen woke to the smell of wet stone and unwashed bodies. The cart’s suspension had groaned one last time before halting waking him up. He had gone in and out of sleep during the trip, but the trip couldn't have taken more than a few hours. They hadn't fed him nor given him any water. 

But it had been long enough for Mr. Halitosis to turn into Meeko. The two black eyes the guard that climbed into the cart was sporting made Caelen feel at least a little better about his own bruises. But it was with that thought that he realized that nothing really hurt. He was a bit sore, but nothing hurt like it did when he first woke up. Every bump in the road he had felt it. But he had eventually slept so either he had passed out or at some point the pain had gotten better.

Speaking in their throaty language Meeko formally known as Mr. Halitosis pulled Caelen to the edge of the cart and let him fall to the ground. Presumably deciding he didn't want to carry Caelen to wherever they were going he cut the binding on his feet. After beating the captive half to death, he likely figured there wasn't any fight left.  Which would explain the shock on his face as Meeko got his nose broken or at least returned to its formerly dislocation by the heel of a foot.  

When he awoke after the beating the next time Caelen found himself in a cell with thirty other captives, their forms where indistinct against the gloom. Some were wrapped in rags; others sat bare-chested, skin stained with soot or dried blood. A few eyes met his as he shifted his weight, testing the range of motion allowed.

The strangest part though was the positioning of the others in the cell. He was laying at the cell door. Caelen could only assume in the exact location he was dropped. As he uncurled his cramped muscles he hurt but not nearly enough. He had just been kicked unconscious twice in a short period, but nothing was broken, breathing only gave a slight twinge of pain and all the muscles so far had worked without cramping. He was in much better shape than he expected.
 
He tried to suppress the rising panic. Fear would get you beaten; indifference might keep you alive for another day. He focused on observation instead of reaction. On the other side of the bars near the cell door stood two guards in dull uniforms, spears resting casually against their shoulders. Their faces were hidden, shadowed by hoods. They moved without urgency, watching not him but someone deeper inside the pen.

On the far side, a man in purple sat at a rickety table seated on an overturned crate. Behind him stood a mamoth of a man with scars all over his upper body in a decretive pattern. These were lumps of scarred flesh that ran in spiralling arcs up his arms across his cheat up his nech and cheaks and across his forehead. They where each perfectly shaped while the ones on his face and hands where significantly smaller then those that ranged across his chest.

The scarred man’s posture betrayed exhaustion, yet he spoke with an air of authority. The purple figure said something I couldnt hear and likely couldnt understand is I did. He had flipped the page of a ledger, his black-tipped cane tapping rhythmically against the stone floor, as if conducting some unseen orchestra of humiliation.

Then came the strike.

A second guard from behind purples other shoulder stepped out and walked across the cell. As soon as he moved the room fell silent. That's when a girl crouching in the corner closest to him looked at him with such fear etched on her face that Caelen felt it. The Guard reached her and swung a cane hard across her shoulders. She cried out—a sound torn between pain and terror. Fresh blood seeped through the brown stains on her tunic as the guard pulled back his arm to strike again.

Her scream caught in Caelens chest like a stone dropped into water. Caelen had frozen for a heartbeat as he watched the first strike fall, but with that scream he forced himself to move. His muscles screamed. He had recovered more than he expected from his last beating but it all still hurt. Something deep inside required he act, it might have been the frightened eyes of a girl clutching a babe to her chest or it might be the fright in eyes of the girl before him but whatever it was, he moved.

In the silence he started crawling to his feet keeping his voice low but steady, he let out a loud "Hey! You want to get rough with someone? I'm all yours!" He was pretty happy they didn't understand him because the line was lame enough that he cringed. 

The guard scoffed, raising the cane again. Caelen kept talking as he finely reached his feet and started over. "Look at that. I’m just guessing here, right? You know how it is out there. Bad guys always pick the easiest targets first." Even though they didn't understand him they had stopped. 

He didn't really have a plan when he started this, but he was locked in now. They were only a few steps away. So naked bruised and barely able to walk in a new body with new gravity he stumbled the few steps and eventually fell over the girl covering her back with his.

Outline:
Purpose: Caelen takes the immediate consequences of covering the injured girl with his own body, choosing to protect her despite having no plan and little strength.

Viewpoint: Third-person limited, Caelen. Begin exactly where approved Beat 2 ends: naked, bruised, stumbling in unfamiliar gravity, he has fallen over the girl and is shielding her back with his. He is not standing aside observing the pen.

Objective: Keep his body between the girl and the guard's cane. Show the guard's immediate response and the physical cost or credible interruption of the threatened blow. Caelen cannot understand the captors' language; dialogue in it must remain unintelligible to him. His awkward shouted challenge was a distraction, not a successful social bluff or bid for status.

Meaningful change: His unplanned protective act makes him the immediate focus of the captors' attention and leaves a concrete consequence for the next scene. Any intervention by the man in purple or the scarred man must arise visibly from this incident, not a detached political contest. Preserve their actual positions: the man in purple at the ledger, the scarred man behind him; the scarred man's status is not established as a captive's.

Continuity dependencies: Approved prose overrides old outlines. The girl being caned is distinct from the remembered girl clutching a babe; do not invent a bundle, rations, or a revelation about an infant. Caelen has recovered surprisingly from earlier beatings but remains sore and physically vulnerable. Do not give him effortless fighting ability, fluent comprehension, a calculated deception strategy, resource-hoarding conclusions, or an unexplained return to passive observation. Do not force self-sacrifice as a rule; show this specific instinctive choice and its consequences. Write only this beat, without recapping the cart ride or replaying his approach to the girl.
Prose:
The floor caught his knees first. Then his shoulder struck the wall, and for a moment all he could do was keep himself from dropping his full weight onto her.

The girl made a small, strangled sound beneath him. Caelen braced his hands against the stone beside her and tried to lift his chest enough to let her breathe. His back was exposed. He knew it was exposed. Knowing did nothing useful about it.

Something hissed through the air.

The cane landed across his shoulder blades.

His arms folded. Pain flashed white behind his eyes, sharp enough to drive every clever thing he might have said out of his head. His cheek scraped the wall. Under him, the girl flinched as though the blow had reached her too.

He sucked in a breath and got almost none of it.

Bad idea. Very bad idea.

The thought arrived with the absurd clarity of a warning delivered after the accident. He could still move. Roll to the side, curl up, make himself small. He had already done that twice today. There was room beside her.

He stayed where he was.

A hand caught his upper arm and hauled. Caelen's knee slid across the wet stone. For one panicked instant he thought they were pulling him clear so the guard could finish what he had started. He dragged his foot back under him, trying to keep some part of himself between the cane and the girl.

The hand tightened.

A voice cut across the cell.

He understood none of it, but the pulling stopped.

Caelen turned his head enough to see the guard looking past him. The cane was raised again, its end dark where it had struck. Across the pen, the man in purple held one hand above his open ledger. His fingers moved once, impatiently.

The guard answered. Whatever he said was short and hard.

The black tip of the other man's cane struck the floor.

Silence followed.

Caelen waited for the next blow. His back had begun to throb in time with his pulse. He couldn't tell whether the warmth spreading toward his ribs was blood or sweat, and he wasn't about to reach around and check.

The grip on his arm loosened. Boots withdrew a step.

Only then did he realize the girl had both hands clenched around the edge of his forearm. Her nails pressed into his skin. He looked down, searching her face for some indication of what he should do next, but she was watching the cane.

"Yeah," he whispered. "Me too."

The man in purple said something else. This time he was looking directly at Caelen.

Behind him, the scarred man shifted away from the wall.

Caelen tried to straighten. His shoulder refused, and he settled back onto one knee, still close enough to cover the girl if the guard changed his mind.

Apparently he had their attention now.
